title: You're Not a Bum
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: Dave Stuart Jr. uses Rocky's persistent fear of being a 'bum' as a mirror for the self-doubt many teachers harbor. Just as Rocky obsesses over proof of his worth despite his efforts and intentions, teachers often internalize self-criticism and doubt about their effectiveness, focusing on outcomes they cannot fully control. Stuart argues that a professional and honest attempt to help students grow—focusing on controllable process and effort rather than uncontrollable outcomes—is sufficient evidence that a teacher is doing meaningful work. The piece offers simple reassurance rooted in locus of control theory: teachers who invest genuine effort in their craft are not failures, regardless of whether every student achieves at the highest level.
points: Teachers, like Rocky, often internalize a fear of being 'bums'—a persistent self-doubt about their value and effectiveness that can paralyze even dedicated professionals in their work. The fundamental error is focusing on outcomes (student achievement, career progression, external validation) rather than controllables (effort, process, professional integrity, planning). A simple but powerful reframe: if a teacher has attempted honestly and professionally to help students grow in knowledge, ability, and wisdom, that teacher has done meaningful work, regardless of statistical outcomes. Teaching efficacy is determined by commitment to process and effort, not by perfect outcomes, which are shaped by factors beyond a teacher's control (student background, family support, external circumstances). Reassurance rooted in locus of control theory provides psychological resilience: focusing on what teachers can actually control liberates them from paralyzing self-doubt and enables sustained professional engagement.
quotes: Fear of being a 'bum' is the core demon of Rocky's life. He's obsessed with bum-ness. Perhaps, lots of us teachers do.
If you've attempted today to help your students grow in strength or knowledge or ability or wisdom, you are, in fact, not a bum.
We control process and effort, not outcomes. It's from a focus on the controllables that you can arrive at this simple conclusion.
